 Aaron Donald will feast against Chargers’ battered offensive line 
 By 
 Michael Duarte 
 Published 
 Nov. 1, 2026, 8:00 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make California Post a Preferred Source 
 In 2018, there were three guarantees in life: death, taxes and Aaron Donald getting a sack. 
 The three-time Defensive Player of the Year Award winner had a career-high 20.5 sacks that season, just two shy of the NFL record at the time. 
 Flash forward eight years and Donald is still searching for his first sack of the 2026 season.

 4 
 LA Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, right, has spent the season behind a patchwork protection unit.  AP Photo/Gregory Bull 
 After nearly three years off, Donald came out of retirement before the season began, and seven weeks into his improbable comeback he’s yet to officially take down the opposing quarterback. He’s had tackles for loss, fumble recoveries, hurries and hits, but his signature moment everyone has been waiting for has yet to arrive. 
 That’s all about to change on Sunday. 
 The Chargers are bringing a battered offensive line into the second-ever matchup between the two SoFi Stadium co-tenants this Sunday. They’ve surrendered 21 sacks through their first seven games. Quarterback Justin Herbert has spent much of the season trying to survive behind a patchwork protection unit that at one point had four rookies starting. 
 Now, the Bolts’ offensive line is tasked with the difficult assignment of trying to stop arguably the greatest interior defensive lineman in NFL history as he seeks his first sack of the season. 
 It’s the kind of matchup Donald used to feast on during the prime of his career and we’re betting the old Aaron Donald finally makes an appearance in the “Battle for Los Angeles .” 
 Despite Donald’s numbers this season, he’s still been effective for the Rams, especially considering all of their injuries to the interior defense. 
 4 
 Aaron Donald is still searching for his first sack of the 2026 season. Getty Images 
 Donald has never needed a statistician to validate his greatness. His 111 career sacks and eight first-team All-Pro selections already secured his place among football’s immortals.
 But Donald isn’t chasing another individual accolade. He made that abundantly clear this week when asked about his statistical production.
 “I ain’t come back for no individual stats,” Donald said. “My main focus is trying to find ways to help this team win. The only thing that excites me is winning.”
 In Donald’s defense, there have been several occasions this season where he sacked the quarterback only to have the play negated by a penalty on the Rams’ defense. 
 But Donald doesn’t care whether he records a sack. At 35 years old, he no longer has anything to prove, which makes him an especially dangerous player. He isn’t chasing sack totals or personal milestones. He’s chasing victories, and the Rams desperately need another one after salvaging their season with a 35–21 win over the Raiders last Sunday. 
 4 
 Donald has spent weeks rediscovering the rhythm that made him a nightmare for offensive coordinators. AP Photo/Katie Chin 
 The Chargers’ offensive line has been ravaged by injuries, forcing inexperienced players into responsibilities they might not otherwise have assumed. But Donald isn’t overlooking anyone.
 He specifically praised the Chargers’ young offensive linemen, identifying tackle Travis Burke and guard Logan Taylor as two players who stood out to him during film review. But when asked what specifically he sees on tape that will help him gain an advantage against them, he remained secretive. 
 “I’m not going to tell you that. We’re not going to tell anyone,” laughed Donald. “Yeah, we see a lot of things, but that’s why you study, right? We have the answers to the test, now we have to pass.”
 That’s not a player looking for an easy afternoon. That’s a veteran who understands that underestimating an opponent is the quickest way to get embarrassed.
 For a player who has spent his career studying offensive linemen like a scientist examining a specimen, that statement should make Herbert uncomfortable.
 4 
 While Donald’s first sack this season has remained elusive, his presence creates opportunities for others. AP Photo/Katie Chin 
 “He’s always watching tape,” said Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula, who has watched Donald for years. “I walked in, it was during lunch, and he was sitting there on his iPad watching tape. I remember him doing that when he was a player 10 years ago.”
 That obsession helped turn an undersized defensive tackle from Pittsburgh into one of the most feared players of his generation.
 And while Donald’s first sack this season has remained elusive, his presence still creates opportunities for everyone around him.
 The Chargers cannot afford to block Donald 1-on-1 throughout Sunday’s game. Sending a second blocker his direction, however, creates favorable matchups for Braden Fiske, Byron Young and the rest of the Rams’ pass rush.
 With Kobie Turner and Poona Ford sidelined, Donald’s ability to command attention becomes even more valuable.
 If Herbert spends Sunday escaping pressure from Donald only to run into another Rams defender, that’s still a victory for Los Angeles.
 But we don’t believe Donald will have to settle for being a decoy.
 The timing is too perfect, the matchup too inviting and the opportunity too significant.
 Donald has spent weeks rediscovering the rhythm that made him a nightmare for offensive coordinators. He’s getting more comfortable, more explosive and more familiar with the speed of the game.
 Now comes a wounded Chargers offensive line and a quarterback who has already been sacked 21 times.
 We predict that Donald will finally break through on Sunday, record his first sack since coming out of retirement and remind the NFL why opposing quarterbacks spent a decade checking where No. 99 lined up before every snap.
